e-491.knowledge_point: Using Integration by Parts to Compute an Indefinite Integral Containing an Exponential Expression
e-491.worked_solution:
To solve this integral, we use the by-parts formula, given by

$$
\int uv' \, \textrm{d}x= uv - \int vu' \, \textrm{d}x.
$$

We need to express $\displaystyle  \int xe^{7x} \textrm{d}x$ as $\displaystyle  \int uv'\,\textrm{d}x.$ Therefore, we set

$$
\begin{aligned}u=x\, & ⟹\,{u}^{′}=1 \\ {v}^{′}={e}^{7x}\, & ⟹\,v=\frac{1}{7}{e}^{7x}.\end{aligned}
$$

We substitute the above into the integration by parts formula, and we get the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}\int u{v}^{′}\,\text{d}x & =uv-\int v{u}^{′}\,\text{d}x \\ \int x\cdot {e}^{7x}\,\text{d}x & =x\cdot \frac{1}{7}{e}^{7x}-\int \frac{1}{7}{e}^{7x}\cdot 1\,\text{d}x\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we calculate the integral:

$$
\begin{aligned}\int x{e}^{7x}\,\text{d}x & =\frac{1}{7}x{e}^{7x}-\frac{1}{7}\int {e}^{7x}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{1}{7}x{e}^{7x}-\frac{1}{7}(\frac{{e}^{7x}}{7})+C \\  & =\frac{1}{7}x{e}^{7x}-\frac{1}{49}{e}^{7x}+C\end{aligned}
$$

decision.explanation: Integration by parts with u=3x and dv=e^{-x} dx gives v=-e^{-x}, so the integral is -3xe^{-x}+3∫e^{-x} dx=-3xe^{-x}-3e^{-x}+C. Differentiating confirms 3xe^{-x}.

after.worked_solution:
To solve this integral, we use the by-parts formula, given by

$$
\int u{v}^{′}\,\text{d}x=uv-\int v{u}^{′}\,\text{d}x.
$$

We need to express $\int 3x{e}^{-x}\text{d}x$ as $\int u{v}^{′}\,\text{d}x.$ Therefore, we set

$$
\begin{aligned}u=3x\, & ⟹\,{u}^{′}=3 \\ {v}^{′}={e}^{-x}\, & ⟹\,v=-{e}^{-x}.\end{aligned}
$$

We substitute the above into the integration by parts formula, and we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\int u{v}^{′}\,\text{d}x & =uv-\int v{u}^{′}\,\text{d}x \\ \int 3x\cdot {e}^{-x}\,\text{d}x & =3x\cdot (-{e}^{-x})-\int (-{e}^{-x})\cdot 3\,\text{d}x.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we calculate the integral, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\int 3x{e}^{-x}\,\text{d}x & =-3x{e}^{-x}+3\int {e}^{-x}\,\text{d}x \\  & =-3x{e}^{-x}-3{e}^{-x}+C\end{aligned}
$$

Question 1

Calculate the integral ∫3xe−xdx.

a
2e−x−3xe−x+C
b
−3xe−x+e−x+C
c
3e−x−xe−x+C
d
−3xe−x−2e−x+C
e
−3xe−x−3e−x+C
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

To solve this integral, we use the by-parts formula, given by

∫uv′dx=uv−∫vu′dx.

We need to express ∫3xe−xdx as ∫uv′dx. Therefore, we set

u=3x⟹u′=3v′=e−x⟹v=−e−x.

We substitute the above into the integration by parts formula, and we get ∫uv′dx=uv−∫vu′dx∫3x⋅e−xdx=3x⋅(−e−x)−∫(−e−x)⋅3dx.

Finally, we calculate the integral, as follows:

∫3xe−xdx=−3xe−x+3∫e−xdx=−3xe−x−3e−x+C

To solve this integral, we use the by-parts formula, given by

$$
\int u{v}^{′}\,\text{d}x=uv-\int v{u}^{′}\,\text{d}x.
$$

We need to express $\int 3x{e}^{-x}\text{d}x$ as $\int u{v}^{′}\,\text{d}x.$ Therefore, we set

$$
\begin{aligned}u=3x\, & ⟹\,{u}^{′}=3 \\ {v}^{′}={e}^{-x}\, & ⟹\,v=-{e}^{-x}.\end{aligned}
$$

We substitute the above into the integration by parts formula, and we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\int u{v}^{′}\,\text{d}x & =uv-\int v{u}^{′}\,\text{d}x \\ \int 3x\cdot {e}^{-x}\,\text{d}x & =3x\cdot (-{e}^{-x})-\int (-{e}^{-x})\cdot 3\,\text{d}x.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we calculate the integral, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\int 3x{e}^{-x}\,\text{d}x & =-3x{e}^{-x}+3\int {e}^{-x}\,\text{d}x \\  & =-3x{e}^{-x}-3{e}^{-x}+C\end{aligned}
$$

decision.explanation: Using integration by parts with u=3x and dv=e^{2x+5} dx gives v=e^{2x+5}/2. Thus the integral is 3xe^{2x+5}/2−(3/2)∫e^{2x+5} dx=3xe^{2x+5}/2−3e^{2x+5}/4+C. Differentiation returns 3xe^{2x+5}.

after.name: Question 2
after.worked_solution:
To solve this integral, we use the by-parts formula, given by

$$
\int u{v}^{′}\,\text{d}x=uv-\int v{u}^{′}\,\text{d}x.
$$

We need to express $\int 3x{e}^{2x+5}\text{d}x$ as $\int u{v}^{′}\,\text{d}x.$ Therefore, we set

$$
\begin{aligned}u=3x\, & ⟹\,{u}^{′}=3 \\ {v}^{′}={e}^{2x+5}\, & ⟹\,v=\frac{{e}^{2x+5}}{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

We substitute the above into the integration by parts formula, and we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\int u{v}^{′}\,\text{d}x & =uv-\int v{u}^{′}\,\text{d}x \\ \int 3x\cdot {e}^{2x+5}\,\text{d}x & =3x\cdot \frac{{e}^{2x+5}}{2}-\int \frac{{e}^{2x+5}}{2}\cdot 3\,\text{d}x.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we calculate the integral, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\int 3x{e}^{2x+5}\,\text{d}x & =\frac{3x{e}^{2x+5}}{2}-\frac{3}{2}\int {e}^{2x+5}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{3x{e}^{2x+5}}{2}-\frac{3{e}^{2x+5}}{4}+C\end{aligned}
$$

content.worked_solution:
To solve this integral, we use the by-parts formula, given by

$$
\int u{v}^{′}\,\text{d}x=uv-\int v{u}^{′}\,\text{d}x.
$$

We need to express $\int 3x{e}^{2x+5}\text{d}x$ as $\int u{v}^{′}\,\text{d}x.$ Therefore, we set

$$
\begin{aligned}u=3x\, & ⟹\,{u}^{′}=3 \\ {v}^{′}={e}^{2x+5}\, & ⟹\,v=\frac{{e}^{2x+5}}{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

We substitute the above into the integration by parts formula, and we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\int u{v}^{′}\,\text{d}x & =uv-\int v{u}^{′}\,\text{d}x \\ \int 3x\cdot {e}^{2x+5}\,\text{d}x & =3x\cdot \frac{{e}^{2x+5}}{2}-\int \frac{{e}^{2x+5}}{2}\cdot 3\,\text{d}x.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we calculate the integral, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\int 3x{e}^{2x+5}\,\text{d}x & =\frac{3x{e}^{2x+5}}{2}-\frac{3}{2}\int {e}^{2x+5}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{3x{e}^{2x+5}}{2}-\frac{3{e}^{2x+5}}{4}+C\end{aligned}
$$

decision.explanation: Integration by parts with u=3x+5 and dv=e^{-5x} dx gives v=-e^{-5x}/5. Thus the integral is −(3x+5)e^{-5x}/5+(3/5)∫e^{-5x} dx=−(3x+5)e^{-5x}/5−3e^{-5x}/25+C, matching option e.

after.name: Question 3
after.worked_solution:
To solve this integral, we use the by-parts formula, given by

$$
\int u{v}^{′}\,\text{d}x=uv-\int v{u}^{′}\,\text{d}x.
$$

We need to express $\int (3x+5){e}^{-5x}\text{d}x$ as $\int u{v}^{′}\,\text{d}x.$ Therefore, we set

$$
\begin{aligned}u=3x+5\, & ⟹\,{u}^{′}=3 \\ {v}^{′}={e}^{-5x}\, & ⟹\,v=-\frac{{e}^{-5x}}{5}.\end{aligned}
$$

We substitute the above into the integration by parts formula, and we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\int u{v}^{′}\,\text{d}x & =uv-\int v{u}^{′}\,\text{d}x \\ \int (3x+5)\cdot {e}^{-5x}\,\text{d}x & =(3x+5)\cdot (-\frac{{e}^{-5x}}{5})-\int (-\frac{{e}^{-5x}}{5})\cdot 3\,\text{d}x.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we calculate the integral, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\int (3x+5){e}^{-5x}\,\text{d}x & =-\frac{(3x+5){e}^{-5x}}{5}+\frac{3}{5}\int {e}^{-5x}\,\text{d}x \\  & =-\frac{(3x+5){e}^{-5x}}{5}-\frac{3{e}^{-5x}}{25}+C\end{aligned}
$$

To solve this integral, we use the by-parts formula, given by

$$
\int u{v}^{′}\,\text{d}x=uv-\int v{u}^{′}\,\text{d}x.
$$

We need to express $\int (3x+5){e}^{-5x}\text{d}x$ as $\int u{v}^{′}\,\text{d}x.$ Therefore, we set

$$
\begin{aligned}u=3x+5\, & ⟹\,{u}^{′}=3 \\ {v}^{′}={e}^{-5x}\, & ⟹\,v=-\frac{{e}^{-5x}}{5}.\end{aligned}
$$

We substitute the above into the integration by parts formula, and we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\int u{v}^{′}\,\text{d}x & =uv-\int v{u}^{′}\,\text{d}x \\ \int (3x+5)\cdot {e}^{-5x}\,\text{d}x & =(3x+5)\cdot (-\frac{{e}^{-5x}}{5})-\int (-\frac{{e}^{-5x}}{5})\cdot 3\,\text{d}x.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we calculate the integral, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\int (3x+5){e}^{-5x}\,\text{d}x & =-\frac{(3x+5){e}^{-5x}}{5}+\frac{3}{5}\int {e}^{-5x}\,\text{d}x \\  & =-\frac{(3x+5){e}^{-5x}}{5}-\frac{3{e}^{-5x}}{25}+C\end{aligned}
$$

decision.explanation: Integration by parts with u=6x and dv=e^{4x} dx gives v=e^{4x}/4. Therefore the integral is 3xe^{4x}/2−(3/2)∫e^{4x} dx=3xe^{4x}/2−3e^{4x}/8+C, matching option b.

after.name: Question 4
after.worked_solution:
To solve this integral, we use the by-parts formula, given by

$$
\int u{v}^{′}\,\text{d}x=uv-\int v{u}^{′}\,\text{d}x.
$$

We need to express $\int 6x{e}^{4x}\text{d}x$ as $\int u{v}^{′}\,\text{d}x.$ Therefore, we set

$$
\begin{aligned}u=6x\, & ⟹\,{u}^{′}=6 \\ {v}^{′}={e}^{4x}\, & ⟹\,v=\frac{1}{4}{e}^{4x}.\end{aligned}
$$

We substitute the above into the integration by parts formula, and we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\int u{v}^{′}\,\text{d}x & =uv-\int v{u}^{′}\,\text{d}x \\ \int 6x\cdot {e}^{4x}\,\text{d}x & =6x\cdot \frac{1}{4}{e}^{4x}-\int \frac{1}{4}{e}^{4x}\cdot 6\,\text{d}x.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we calculate the integral, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\int 6x{e}^{4x}\,\text{d}x & =\frac{3}{2}x{e}^{4x}-\frac{3}{2}\int {e}^{4x}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{3x{e}^{4x}}{2}-\frac{3{e}^{4x}}{8}+C\end{aligned}
$$

content.worked_solution:
To solve this integral, we use the by-parts formula, given by

$$
\int u{v}^{′}\,\text{d}x=uv-\int v{u}^{′}\,\text{d}x.
$$

We need to express $\int 6x{e}^{4x}\text{d}x$ as $\int u{v}^{′}\,\text{d}x.$ Therefore, we set

$$
\begin{aligned}u=6x\, & ⟹\,{u}^{′}=6 \\ {v}^{′}={e}^{4x}\, & ⟹\,v=\frac{1}{4}{e}^{4x}.\end{aligned}
$$

We substitute the above into the integration by parts formula, and we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\int u{v}^{′}\,\text{d}x & =uv-\int v{u}^{′}\,\text{d}x \\ \int 6x\cdot {e}^{4x}\,\text{d}x & =6x\cdot \frac{1}{4}{e}^{4x}-\int \frac{1}{4}{e}^{4x}\cdot 6\,\text{d}x.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we calculate the integral, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\int 6x{e}^{4x}\,\text{d}x & =\frac{3}{2}x{e}^{4x}-\frac{3}{2}\int {e}^{4x}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{3x{e}^{4x}}{2}-\frac{3{e}^{4x}}{8}+C\end{aligned}
$$
